clue.text: Game played in Animal Farm?

parts.note: Orwell's farm is run by pigs, so picture a porker standing at the centre of a playground ball game

explanation.surface: A question about what sport the beasts of Orwell's novel might enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: The playground game has one player standing between two others trying to intercept the ball; in Animal Farm the pigs are literally at the centre of things.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a children's ball game where one player tries to intercept throws between two others.

clue.text: Steeplechase jockey in t-top option

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre or shift about, so these letters are jostled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider weighing up a car with a T-top roof as an option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockey' looks like part of the racing picture but is the anagram signal working on IN, TTOP and OPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A point-to-point is an amateur steeplechase race meeting run over a cross-country course in Britain.

clue.text: Board to make progress

definitions.meaning: to board a bus or train is to climb onto it
to advance or prosper, as in getting along in life

explanation.surface: A short instruction to climb aboard and move forward.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to climb aboard a vehicle and to advance or succeed.

clue.text: Manage to come up with set places for the youngsters

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word for manage is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it
a set of things, such as stamps or programmes, is a series

explanation.surface: Advice to organise a collection of venues for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manage' hides the verb run; 'to come up' turns it to NUR, read upward in this down entry. 'set' is a noun here, not the verb it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurseries are rooms or establishments where small children are cared for.

clue.text: Doctor wearing rough-woven headgear

indicators.note: the outer letters wear the doctor's abbreviation like a garment around it
weaving twists strands together, so the letters of rough are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic dons a hat made of coarse homespun cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough-woven' looks like a description of the hat's cloth, but 'woven' rearranges ROUGH as HOURG and 'wearing' wraps that around the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A homburg is a felt hat with a dented crown and curled brim, a kind of headgear.

clue.text: Ornament getting additional endless damage

indicators.note: the word for additional loses its final letter, having no end

parts.note: additional means more, as in more time
a dent is a small piece of damage to a surface

explanation.surface: A decoration that keeps getting further harmed without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the final E to leave MOR. In music an ornament is a decorative flourish on a note, not a trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: A mordent is a musical ornament, a quick alternation between a note and the one below it.

clue.text: Thick wooded valley around the point

indicators.note: the valley word goes around the compass letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a dene is a narrow wooded valley, chiefly in English place names
S, south, is one of the points of the compass

explanation.surface: A dull person found in a forested glen near a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the valley word round the compass point; 'the' is a link word. Dene is a mainly northern English word for a narrow valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense and thick are synonyms, used of fog, foliage or a slow-witted person.

clue.text: Porter's room intended, say, for deposit of monies

parts.note: a college or building porter works from a lodge by the entrance

indicators.note: say signals that the word for intended is spoken and its sound written down

parts.note: intended means meant, as in meant well

explanation.surface: The porter's office is meant to hold banked cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives the sound of MEANT, spelt MENT. In British colleges the porter's lodge is the gatehouse office by the entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodgement is the act of lodging money, a deposit placed in a bank or with an authority.

clue.text: Post Office missed out of guide to Bury

indicators.note: the Post Office letters are left out from the word for guide

parts.note: a pointer is a guide or hint showing the way

explanation.surface: A postal branch is absent from a directory to the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' poses as the Lancashire town; it is the verb, the definition. Removing PO from POINTER leaves INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body in a grave.

clue.text: Confused dame in a right pickle

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled elderly lady finds herself in real trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' reads as a predicament; it is the brine meat is soaked in.
explanation.definitionFit: A marinade is a seasoned liquid for soaking food, a kind of pickle.

clue.text: Hurry up tramp with the fuel

parts.note: to tramp on something is to step on it heavily
taken as written
gas is fuel, and American for petrol

explanation.surface: Urging a vagrant to hurry along with his fuel can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' poses as a vagrant but is the verb, giving STEP ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To step on the gas is to press the accelerator, an idiom for hurrying.

clue.text: Aunt with one unusual car cover

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aunt with a strange vehicle tarpaulin.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNT and ONE together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonneau is a flexible cover stretched over the open rear seats or load bed of a vehicle.

clue.text: If you're in yours, it's bliss!

definitions.text: If you're in yours, it's bliss!

parts.words: If you're in yours, it's bliss!
parts.note: an idiom for being completely at home and happy, as a fish in water

explanation.surface: A cheery remark that being in one's own place is perfect happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'in one's element' means being in the situation that suits you best.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in one's element is an idiom for being in surroundings where one is happiest.

clue.text: Some probe literature for old manuscript marks

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scholar examines writings looking for ancient annotation signs.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in prOBE LIterature. The draft put 'for' in the definition; it is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger-shaped marks used in ancient manuscripts to flag doubtful passages.

clue.text: Telling the result I have

parts.note: an effect is a result or outcome
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Announcing the outcome I possess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling' looks like a verb of speech; it is the adjective meaning striking.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling argument is effective, having a striking impact.

clue.text: Drop off wrong goose pelt

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong order, so they need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Discarding a poorly made goose skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop off' reads as discarding; it is dozing.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is an idiom for falling asleep.

clue.text: Deliberately destroys footwear over a long period

indicators.note: in a down clue, the shoe sits above the period of time

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden clog
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks shoes for years on end.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend links sabotage to workers throwing clogs (sabots) into machines.
explanation.definitionFit: To sabotage is to wreck something on purpose, often to obstruct an enemy.

clue.text: Confuse old boy's pet, caught by explosive device

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: the pet is held within the device word, caught inside it

parts.note: a fuse sets off an explosive charge
a cat is a common pet

explanation.surface: Bewildering a former pupil whose cat is trapped by a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' puts the pet inside the device, making FUSCATE; the 's of 'old boy's' is a link, not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To obfuscate is to make obscure or unclear, so to confuse.

clue.text: One is taken up in this rescue operation

definitions.text: One is taken up in this rescue operation

parts.words: One is taken up in this rescue operation
parts.note: someone is lifted into the sky, by helicopter or plane, to save them

explanation.surface: Describing a rescue in which a person is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' is literal: the rescued person is carried up into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: This rescue transports people or supplies by aircraft, often from an emergency.

clue.text: Editor initially poised, perhaps, for an incident

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word for editor is taken
perhaps suggests poised may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor first appears composed during an incident.
explanation.walkthrough: E then POISED rearranged as PISODE; 'for an' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single event or occurrence, an incident.

clue.text: Stick and stay in the middle

definitions.meaning: a short rod, as carried by a conductor or relay runner
in cricket the middle is the pitch, and a batsman who stays there carries on batting

explanation.surface: Persist and keep to the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'middle' is cricket's pitch: to bat on is to keep batting without getting out.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a stick, and the phrase bat on means continue batting in cricket.

clue.text: Greek character's explicit description of weapon

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
explicit means clear and plain

explanation.surface: A Greek's frank account of armaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'description of weapon' defines an adjective: a nuclear weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a weapon using atomic fission or fusion, as in nuclear bomb.

clue.text: Looking, for example, round a basic principle of Chinese philosophy

indicators.note: the example abbreviation goes round the Chinese principle

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

parts.words: a basic principle of Chinese philosophy
parts.note: yin is the passive feminine principle of Chinese philosophy, paired with yang

explanation.surface: Seeking an example of Chinese thought.
explanation.walkthrough: YIN goes between E and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Eying is watching closely, a form of looking.

clue.text: As a matter of fact, possibly hurt following international

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes after the international abbreviation
possibly says hurt is one possible arrangement of these letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Really, perhaps an injury after a match between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges hurt as RUTH; 'following' places it after the international abbreviation. 'international' is also a match between national sides in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In truth is an idiom meaning actually, really, as a matter of fact.

clue.text: Join in the fun? I tend to!

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is found within the following words

explanation.surface: An invitation to join the fun, eagerly accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are in fUN I TEnd; 'the' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join together as one.

clue.text: Man, we hear, in the round — an islander

indicators.note: we hear means the name is taken as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: Philip is a man's name
taken as written
O is a round shape

explanation.surface: A fellow, so it is said, standing in a circle is from an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The name Philip spoken gives FILIP, then IN and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A Filipino is a native of the Philippines, an island nation.

clue.text: Leaving the state of the ground

definitions.meaning: in horse racing, the condition of the turf, such as good or soft

explanation.surface: Departing from a racecourse after checking the turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Going is departing, and in racing it is the condition of the track surface.

clue.text: Condition to be met by a space traveller

definitions.text: Condition to be met by a space traveller

parts.words: Condition to be met by a space traveller
parts.note: reads like a requirement for astronauts, but it is the state they encounter when gravity seems absent

explanation.surface: A rule an astronaut must satisfy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Condition to be met' suggests a requirement; it is the state encountered in orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts in orbit experience the absence of apparent weight, floating freely.
